name: Light Hunt - Now Playing
author: Light Hunt (lightshunt.com)
description: Shows the song Falcon Player is playing on your display page at lightshunt.com. After you pair it with a code, a small background process reads FPP's local status every 5 seconds and sends the current song (title and artist tags, audio file name, sequence name, play state, time remaining and total length, playlist name) plus the plugin version to lightshunt.com. The only other thing it can send is feedback you write, and only when you press Send on the plugin page. Nothing else leaves this device and the plugin never controls your show.

privacy.summary: Once paired, sends the song now playing, its artist and time left, the next songs, and the playlist name to lightshunt.com. This appears on your public Light Hunt display page.

sends.what: pairing key, song title and artist, file names, play state, time left, the next songs in the playlist, playlist name, plugin version
sends.why: to show what is playing on your public Light Hunt display page

sends.what: plugin version, then the pairing code and a device secret to check it
sends.why: to link this player to your Light Hunt display

sends.what: your feedback message, an email address only if you type one, plugin, FPP and PHP versions, whether paired, the last send result, reason and time, the last 20 plugin log lines only if you tick the box (home folder names, IP addresses and pairing keys removed), and the pairing key as a sign-in header when paired
sends.why: to send feedback to Light Hunt, only when you press Send on the plugin page

collects.what: Light Hunt pairing key and display name, and this player's hardware id (read from Falcon Player, never sent) to notice a copied SD card
pairing code and device secret, while pairing
song now playing and send status, for the plugin page
process ID of the running poller
log of pairing, unpairing and failed sends, never the key

systemChanges.what: Runs one background PHP process (the poller) while FPP is running; stops it when FPP stops

privacy.other: Like FPP's own pages, the plugin's web routes ask for no password: anyone who can open this FPP's web pages can start pairing or unpair it and can see the paired display's name. Pairing is refused while already paired. Reads FPP's local API at 127.0.0.1 (status and media tags). Sends nothing until you pair, apart from feedback you press Send on. The key file is mode 0600. Unpair removes the key from this device; uninstalling removes the key, status file and log.
